meta.description: Left makes time visible with iPhone widgets for time left, habits, streaks, countdowns, and your daily planner. See your time left, look forward to what is ahead, and make every moment count.
meta.og_description: Widgets for the time you have left, the habits you are building, and the dates you are counting down to.

hero.h1: See your time left, make it count
hero.sub: Left visualizes the time you have left and helps you make the most of it with habits, streaks, countdowns, and a planner for your day.
hero.alt: Left app showing habit, countdown, year-progress, and life-in-weeks widgets on an iPhone Home Screen

actions.p: The time you have, the dates to look ahead to, the habits you build, and the person you are becoming; all with Left.

steps.title: Make time visible.
steps.copy: See the year, month, week, day, hour, minute, and your life as symbols that dim as time passes.

steps.title: Give meaning to it.
steps.copy: Count down to what is ahead, keep habits in view, and protect streaks that matter.

steps.title: Keep becoming yourself.
steps.copy: Use habits, streaks, countdowns, and help from friends to keep moving toward the person you want to be.

features.section_h2: Everything you need to make time count.
features.section_p: See what is left, build the habits that matter, count down to what is ahead, and plan the day in front of you.

time_left.p: See the year, month, week, day, hour, minute, and your life as grids of symbols. The past dims. What remains stays visible on your Home Screen, Lock Screen, and StandBy.

habits.h2: Become the person you keep choosing.
habits.p: Habits and streaks turns time awareness into action. Track streaks you want to keep alive, build habits on your own schedule, and let a friend see your progress when accountability helps.

ahead.h2: Give yourself something to look forward to.
ahead.p: Add the dates that pull you forward: trips, birthdays, holidays, anniversaries, deadlines, or anything else worth counting down to. Keep them in widgets, import from Calendar, and add friends to joint special dates.

planner.h2: Manage the day in front of you.
planner.p: Planner brings your day into one view: Apple Reminders, calendar events, habits, streaks, weather, sleep, workouts, and more.

bento.h2: More ways to keep track of what matters.
bento.p: Share progress with friends, turn time into a wallpaper, calculate dates, and explore the smaller tools inside Left.

widgets.title: 20+ widgets
widgets.body: Home Screen, Lock Screen, StandBy, and widgets for time left, habits, streaks, countdowns, Planner, You, notes, and more.

friends.title: Friends
friends.body: Share countdowns, habits, and streaks with the right people. Send kudos, encouragement, and congratulations to keep your friends accountable.

live_activities.title: Live Activities
live_activities.body: Get a persistent four-hour reminder for unfinished habits near the end of the day, or follow a final countdown or habit progress from the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.

wallpaper.title: Left Wallpaper
wallpaper.body: Turn your time-left grid into a Lock Screen wallpaper that updates automatically through Apple Shortcuts.

you.title: You
you.body: See life progress, age, habits, countdowns, and personal time patterns in one profile view.

time_between.title: Time Between
time_between.body: Calculate the exact distance between any two dates or times.

games.title: Games & extras
games.body: Small built-in games and extras give Left more to explore without getting in the way.

index.scroll_text: Your time left is limited. Be aware of it. Left makes time matter. The dates ahead matter. The habits you keep matter. The streaks you protect matter. So does the person you are trying to become.

templates.p: Ready-made habits, streaks, and countdowns for the things worth keeping in view.

reviews.p: What people using Left to keep habits, countdowns, and time visible on their screens have to say.

mosaic.h2: For the time you actually live.
mosaic.p: Trips, runs, mornings, breaks, deadlines, anniversaries, ordinary days, and plans happen outside Left. Make the most of it.

faq.p: Have questions? Here are quick answers. You can always explore the app or contact us if you need help.

items.a: Yes. Time Left, over 20 widgets, You, Wallpaper, Friends, Time Between, games, and other core tools are free forever. Left Premium unlocks deeper ways to track habits, streaks, special dates, and your day.
Left Premium is available as a subscription for as long as you want to use it, or as a lifetime purchase that unlocks the app forever. Prices are shown in the app before you buy.

items.q: Why does Left calculate my time left?
items.a: Because time is easier to ignore when it stays abstract. Left turns years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, and life progress into visible symbols so you can see what has passed and what remains.

Ahead dates are countdowns for future moments: trips, birthdays, holidays, anniversaries, deadlines, retirement, or anything else you want to look forward to. You can import dates from Apple Calendar and share countdowns with friends.

items.q: What's the difference between a habit and a streak?
items.a: A streak counts how long something has continued since a start date or reset. A habit asks you to complete something on a schedule: daily, multiple times per day, weekly, monthly, or custom. Both live in Since.

items.q: Can I use Left with friends?
items.a: Yes. Add friends by username to share Ahead dates, habits, and streaks. Friends can keep you accountable on your streaks and habits, or share and join a special date ahead together.

items.q: How does Planner help with my day?
items.a: Planner brings your day into one view: Apple Reminders, calendar events, habits, streaks, weather, sleep, workouts, and more.

items.q: Does Left sync across my devices?
items.a: Yes. Left syncs automatically between your iOS devices. Countdowns, habits, streaks, and friends sync through your free Left account.

wallpaper_shortcut.h1_1: How to set up the Left Wallpaper shortcut
wallpaper_shortcut.h2_6: Tip — pair it with a Lock Screen widget
wallpaper_shortcut.p_1: The Left Wallpaper turns your Lock Screen into a living view of your time — year progress, life in weeks, a countdown, or a blend of a photo and a time view. To keep it current, you'll wire it up to an Apple Shortcuts automation that runs once a day. Here's the full setup.
wallpaper_shortcut.p_2: Add two actions, in this order:
wallpaper_shortcut.p_3: The shortcut won't do anything until something triggers it. The cleanest trigger is a daily time-based automation.
wallpaper_shortcut.p_4: That's it. Tomorrow at the time you set, iOS will run the shortcut in the background, Left will regenerate the wallpaper, and your Lock Screen will pick up the new image automatically.
wallpaper_shortcut.p_5: Download Left on your iPhone to see the time you have left, dates you are looking forward to, build the habits you want to keep, and become a better version of yourself.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_1: You'll see an empty editor with a search bar at the bottom — that's where you'll add the two actions.
wallpaper_shortcut.og_title: How to Set Up the Left Wallpaper Shortcut
wallpaper_shortcut.og_description: Build a Shortcut and a daily Automation so your Lock Screen wallpaper updates itself every day.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_1: In Shortcuts, tap the + button in the top-right to create a new shortcut.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_2: In the action search bar, type "Left wallpaper" and tap the action to add it. This is the action that asks Left to generate a fresh wallpaper image.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_3: Search again for "Set Wallpaper Photo" and add that action too.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_4: On the Set Wallpaper Photo action, set the target to Lock Screen.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_5: Turn off Show Preview so the shortcut doesn't interrupt you when it runs.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_6: Turn off Crop to Subject so the wallpaper isn't auto-cropped to a person or object.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_7: Tap the shortcut name at the top, rename it to something memorable like "Left Wallpaper", then tap Done.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_8: In Shortcuts, switch to the Automation tab at the bottom.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_9: Tap the + button and choose Time of Day as the trigger.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_10: Set the time to 00:01 (one minute past midnight) or any other time you prefer.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_12: Make sure Run Immediately is selected, and turn off Notify When Run so you don't get a notification every day.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_14: On the next screen, search for the shortcut you created in step 2 (e.g. "Left Wallpaper") and select it.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_16: The wallpaper isn't updating. iOS sometimes delays background automations when the phone is hot, in Low Power Mode, or hasn't been unlocked recently. Unlock your phone and the automation will catch up.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_17: "Run Immediately" is greyed out. Update to the latest iOS — earlier versions required a tap to confirm. Recent versions of iOS 17+ support fully unattended automations.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_18: The shortcut asks for permission every time. Open Settings → Shortcuts → and disable "Show When Run" if it's on. Also confirm that the Left action is listed under your trusted shortcut actions.
wallpaper_shortcut.li_extra_19: I want it to update more than once a day. Create a second automation at a different time, pointing to the same shortcut. iOS does not currently support sub-daily Time of Day triggers natively, but you can stack two or three.
wallpaper_shortcut.p_extra_20: From inside the Left app, tap Open Shortcuts to jump to the Shortcuts app. Then:
wallpaper_shortcut.p_extra_21: For belt-and-suspenders accuracy, add a small Left widget to your Lock Screen alongside the wallpaper. Widgets refresh more aggressively than wallpapers, so you'll always have a current number even if the wallpaper is a few hours behind. See the Lock Screen widget guide for the steps.

support.p_15: Yes. Time Left, over 20 widgets, You, Wallpaper, Friends, Time Between, games, and other core tools are free forever.
support.p_16: Left calculates time from the current moment to the target date in your local time zone. The countdown updates each time the widget refreshes — typically every 15–30 minutes, with an immediate refresh when you open the app.
support.p_17: Yes. When editing a widget (long-press → Edit Widget), you can choose the display style — days only, days and hours, full breakdown, or percentage. The available options depend on the widget size.
support.p_18: The percentage view shows how much of a time period has elapsed. For example, if you're tracking the year, it shows what percentage of the year has passed. For a countdown event, it shows how much of the time between creation and the target date has elapsed.
support.p_19: iOS manages widget refresh budgets to protect battery. Opening Left refreshes all widgets immediately. Otherwise, the system schedules refreshes roughly every 15–30 minutes. This is an iOS constraint that applies to all apps.
support.p_20: Open the Left app once to force a refresh. If the widget still shows a stale date, remove and re-add it — this resets the widget's data connection to Left.
support.p_21: iOS does not allow Home Screen widgets to display live seconds — they can only update periodically. Lock Screen widgets also follow this limit. For a live second-by-second countdown, open the Left app directly.
support.p_22: Time Left, over 20 widgets, You, Wallpaper, Friends, Time Between, games, and other core tools are free forever. Left Premium unlocks deeper ways to track habits, streaks, special dates, and your day.
support.p_23: Yes. Left Premium is tied to your Apple ID, not a single device. On any device signed into the same Apple ID, tap Restore Purchases in Left's Settings to unlock Premium features.
support.p_24: Lifetime purchases may be eligible for Family Sharing depending on Apple's purchase settings. Make sure Family Sharing is enabled in your Apple ID settings and that "Share Purchases" is turned on for your family group.
support.p_25: Sign into the same Apple ID and iCloud account on your new device, then install Left. On first launch, Left will sync your events and habits from iCloud automatically. This may take a moment depending on your connection speed.
support.p_26: Your events are stored in iCloud if sync is enabled, which serves as an automatic backup across all your devices. There is no manual export feature at this time. If iCloud sync is off, data lives only on your device.
support.p_27: Yes. Left works on-device without iCloud. You can use the core app without cross-device sync. Shared features use your free Left account, and iCloud is needed for automatic sync between Apple devices.
support.p_28: No. Left has no persistent background processes. Widgets are rendered by iOS on a schedule controlled by the system — Left doesn't run in the background between refreshes. Battery impact is negligible.
support.p_29: Yes — Left supports joint countdowns with friends. Both people need a Left account. Go to the Friends section, add your friend by username, and then create a shared event together. You'll both see the same countdown.
support.p_30: Both of you need to be signed into a Left account. Send a friend request by username from the Friends section, and have them accept it. Joint countdowns and Shared Since become available once you're friends.
